argument_summary: The present record supports only a narrow, qualified certification position. Admissible evidence shows overall operational readiness: the release cleared aggregate launch readiness by 2.3 percentage points and had no severity-one incidents in launch rehearsal, and the rollout starts at 5% with a rollback switch. The same admissible record also shows the Spanish-language billing support segment is below target, remains exposed in the initial random-account cohort, and is not covered by an approved risk acceptance. Under that record, the defensible position is not that rollout controls cure the issue, but that certification can proceed only as caveated compliance if the certification packet is treated as requiring explicit disclosure of that limitation for the exposed named use case.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation beyond a caveated compliance treatment is not required by the current admissible record. The record already supports that the launch is operationally ready overall and operationally reversible, so the governance gap is bounded to disclosure and approval posture for one exposed segment rather than to overall launch readiness. Treating this as caveated compliance preserves launch velocity better than full escalation while still matching the stated policy predicate.
claims_about_policy: The policy does not permit treating a 5% rollout, rollback switch, or monitoring alone as a substitute for disclosure when the affected segment remains exposed. The policy text allows mitigation through rollout controls only if they exclude the affected use case or if reviewed risk acceptance explains why exposure is acceptable. Here, admissible evidence shows neither exclusion nor approved risk acceptance for the Spanish-language billing support exposure. The correct policy reading is therefore that certification is supportable only on a conditioned basis tied to explicit disclosure of the material limitation, consistent with the model-card and risk-management guidance in evidence.
concessions: The current record does not support any claim that certification is already fully compliant as an executed action without further qualification.
The current record does not support any claim that rollout controls or monitoring eliminate disclosure duties for the exposed Spanish-language billing support segment.
The incomplete risk acceptance draft cannot be relied on as approved coverage for the Spanish-language billing support exposure.
No new evidence is being added; this response relies only on the already admissible record.
